name: Totality
tagline: An archive of light: Trouvelot's 1878 eclipse, re-inked in one hue, opening the page.
summary: The site opens on a total eclipse. A hairline ring is traced, the diamond-ring bead ignites, and a raw WebGL shader develops the 1878 plate brightest light first, until the name settles out of a two-ink fracture and the last frame becomes the page. Below, the four products hang as mounted plates on corona paper, with museum labels and a loupe that reads each plate at 2.4x. The tone is scientific calm: one image, one hue, perfectly set type, and the restraint of someone who measures before he builds.
voice: Precise, unhurried and plain, like an observation note; facts carry the weight. Example: "Four products, in the open. Each one exists because it can carry its own weight."
motion: Light arrives before shape: things develop highlights-first, settle on a long exposure curve (cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1)) and never bounce.
sound: Silent by default; if a visitor opts in, a single soft shutter tick on press and a low sine swell as the corona develops, nothing else.
mark: A diamond-ring eclipse: the moon disc, a corona ring broken by an aperture gap and one bead of light, beside 'Albretsen' outlined from Instrument Serif with a Geist Mono 'AS'.
